headline_marked: [[Elon Musk says SpaceX and xAI will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs]] for AI, deploying Vera Rubin NVL72 in space next year
headline: Elon Musk says SpaceX and xAI will exclusively use Nvidia GPUs for AI, deploying Vera Rubin NVL72 in space next year
summary: Musk cited Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 architecture as "the best AI computer," praising its cable-less design for improved serviceability and reliability.
details: Elon Musk announced that SpaceX and xAI will exclusively build on Nvidia GPUs, citing the Vera Rubin architecture as "the best AI computer." This decision underscores a strong partnership, moving forward with Nvidia's advanced hardware.

Musk specifically praised the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale system's design, highlighting its cable-less compute trays. This design significantly improves serviceability, assembly speed, and reliability by reducing common installation errors.

Historically, xAI has relied on Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell hardware for training Grok, making this official exclusivity largely a formal endorsement. While AMD has used Grok-1 on its Instinct MI300X, there's no public evidence of xAI using non-Nvidia accelerators in production.

SpaceX plans to deploy the optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 computer not only in ground data centers but also in space. This "Starmind AI satellite" is expected to begin launching next year, representing an ambitious project beyond Nvidia's current space deployment plans.

The NVL72 system, featuring 36 Vera CPUs and 72 Rubin AI GPUs, offers formidable performance. However, deploying such a powerful system in orbit raises questions regarding cooling and long-term reliability in the harsh space environment.
caption:
Elon Musk just declared SpaceX and xAI are going "all in" on Nvidia GPUs. He calls the Vera Rubin architecture "the best AI computer."

Elon Musk announced that SpaceX and xAI will exclusively build on Nvidia GPUs, citing the Vera Rubin architecture as "the best AI computer." This decision underscores a strong partnership, moving forward with Nvidia's advanced hardware.

Musk specifically praised the Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale system's design, highlighting its cable-less compute trays. This design significantly improves serviceability, assembly speed, and reliability by reducing common installation errors.

Historically, xAI has relied on Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell hardware for training Grok, making this official exclusivity largely a formal endorsement. While AMD has used Grok-1 on its Instinct MI300X, there's no public evidence of xAI using non-Nvidia accelerators in production.

SpaceX plans to deploy the optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 computer not only in ground data centers but also in space. This "Starmind AI satellite" is expected to begin launching next year, representing an ambitious project beyond Nvidia's current space deployment plans.

The NVL72 system, featuring 36 Vera CPUs and 72 Rubin AI GPUs, offers formidable performance. However, deploying such a powerful system in orbit raises questions regarding cooling and long-term reliability in the harsh space environment.
